subject: Private deployment readiness: wiring & account activation manifest
messages:
From: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@helixhealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: kevin_procure@helixhealth.com
Date: 2025-08-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment wiring questions

Avery —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. We want to lock down the remaining network and credentials items so our infra team can schedule the rack/port work with our data center partner next week. Please send the minimal "activation manifest" you need from us (network ranges, service accounts, cert rotation window, and any required firewall egress rules).

Also flag anything that would block our ability to spin an air-gapped sandbox for smoke tests (we want to validate model inference at ~128 token baseline).

Attached is our current network diagram (pdf) and a very rough checklist from our end.

Appreciate it — Sam

--
Sam Brooks
Director, Cloud Ops
HelixHealth
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@helixhealth.com>, kevin_procure@helixhealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-17T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment wiring questions

Sam / Kevin —

Thanks, this is perfect context. I pulled together an "activation manifest" we use for private deployments — condensed version below so your infra and procurement teams can move in parallel. I kept it deliberately prescriptive (items we must have before Day 0) and noted the expected owner for each ask. If you prefer I can hand this off as a shared Drive checklist and we can iterate with your infra.

REQUIRED PRELAUNCH ITEMS (HelixHealth owner in parentheses)

1) Network & Reachability
 - NAT/egress: outbound IPv4 range for service callbacks and telemetry: 34.203.112.0/22 (Redwood-owned endpoint pool). (Helix infra to whitelist)
 - Inbound: we do NOT require public inbound. For management plane (optional) provide jumpbox NAT IP(s) for 22/443 access during Day 0 only. (Helix infra)
 - DNS: A records for internal service names you plan to map (tenant-xx.redwood.local). Provide zone & delegated records. (Helix infra)
 - MTU: confirm path MTU >= 1500; report any jumbo frames. (Helix infra)

2) Service Accounts & Keying
 - Service account for build & provisioning with create/list/update on project resources. Provide service account email and granted roles (least privileged). (Helix security)
 - KMS integration: KMS key resource id or HSM endpoint and contact for rotation policy. If using external HSM, share PKCS11 endpoint and certs. (Helix security)

3) Identity & Access
 - SSO integration: SAML metadata or OIDC discovery URL for your IdP; test user for initial onboarding. (Helix SSO admin)
 - SSH bastion: public key for Day 0 engineers (we recommend ephemeral access via SSO). (Helix infra)

4) Firewall & Egress Rules (Helix infra to apply)
 - Allow outbound to: 34.203.112.0/22:443 (control plane API), 52.12.0.0/16:443 (telemetry), and NTP/53. (See full list in attached checklist)
 - Allow internal VLANs to reach the inference cluster control subnet (10.240.0.0/20).

5) Environment & Test Data (Helix product/ops)
 - Sandbox dataset: small sample (anonymized) to run quality smoke tests. Provide S3/HTTPS location and read creds. (Helix product)
 - Expected token profile and peak qps target for Day 0 (e.g., 128 tokens, 50 qps).

6) Compliance & Evidence (Helix legal/security)
 - SOC 2 attestation copy or security questionnaire answers relevant to physical hosting.
 - Data retention requirement (logs/metrics) and any egress data residency constraints.

7) Scheduling & Escalation
 - Preferred Day 0 window (2-hour block): supply three options within next 10 business days.
 - Primary on-call for networking during activation and emergency contact (mobile).

ATTACHMENTS FROM REDWOOD (we will provide):
 - Redwood ingress/egress IP list (CSV)
 - Example SSO metadata template (XML)
 - Minimal port plan (pdf)

NEXT STEPS
 - If you can confirm (1) the Day 0 windows and (2) the person who owns KMS, I will create a shared Drive checklist and loop Ben (Day 0 engineer) and Steph (onboarding PM) to finalize runbook tasks.

If any items are non-starters we can mark them as "deferred" and provide fallbacks (e.g., use temporary TLS tunneling if HSM not available).

Best,
Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-08-17T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fw: Private deployment readiness: wiring & account activation manifest

Avery / Steph —

Looping you both in. Ben will be Day 0 lead for HelixHealth (I noted the 50 qps target — should be easy with a single dedicated pool but want to confirm batch sizes and prefix caching policy before we schedule). Quick asks from my side:

- Can we validate their MTU and egress NAT during our pre-flight window? If they have restrictive NAT or CGNAT it affects our callback retry behaviour.
- If Helix can't provide an HSM endpoint, we should prepare to host keys and enable customer-managed key wrap in our VPC with documented split custody.

I'll take the provisioning checklist and draft the runbook. Avery — once they confirm Day 0 options I can assign tasks and create the runbook card in HS-4521.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
